alex: Heads-up — CI perf check flagged a regression on the rolling canary after merge of PR #4321. p95 latency up ~20% on redis-backed workloads. Pausing rollout now :warning:
triage-bot: [CI] perf-check failed for canary: p95 +21% vs baseline. Report: https://ci.redwood-infra/reports/5623 (automated alert) :rotating_light:
maria: Ugh. Which changes in #4321? I remember kernel routing heuristics were modified and there was a small KV cache TTL tweak in the same window. Could be either. :thinking_face:
sam: I pulled a quick flamegraph from the failing job: `flamegraph-171234` shows a bump in `attn_cpu_kernel::compute` and also a small spike in `kv_lookup::miss_path`. Paste: ```
# top stacks (simplified)
attn_cpu_kernel::compute  44%
batch_coordinator::dispatch 15%
kv_lookup::miss_path 9%
memcpy 6%
```
jen: PR #4319 (separate commit) changed the batching heuristics — it reduces micro-batching when seq-len variance is high. That was meant to lower median latency but might increase tail if kernels aren't optimal. Could interact with kernel selector changes in #4321.
ryan: Agree — there's a known interplay: less batching exposes kernel inefficiencies for some models. We should bisect between the two merges. Can we run `git bisect` across the last 6 commits on canary?
maria: I'm on it. Running a quick bisect on staging workloads with the CI perf harness: ```
git bisect start HEAD v1.8.2
# test script: ./tools/perf_ci_runner --profile=kv-heavy
```
triage-bot: Note: running long bisect — estimated 20m. Will post results. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
(12m later)
maria: Bisect narrowed to commit `6789abc` — kernel-autoselect: choose v2-kernel for medium seqs by default. Reverting that locally returns p95 to baseline.
sam: That's consistent with the flamegraph — the new kernel has higher overhead on our small-KV-miss path. Maybe the kernel's fallback path does extra copying. I attached a heap/alloc snapshot: `alloc_diff.patch` shows +18% memcpy in `kv_miss` branch.
ryan: Given this is a canary and we already paused, I'd advocate reverting the kernel-autoselect commit from the canary rollout and adding an automatic gate: if p95 > baseline * 1.15 OR kv_miss_rate delta > 5% then auto-revert.
pat: We should also add a distribution check for batch sizes in the SLO guardrail — if the 95th percentile of batch_size decreases by >10% (indicating more fragmentation), we shouldn't allow kernel switches that assume larger batches.
alex: +1 to revert now. Also opening a short-term mitigation: pin kernel selector to `v1.9-kernel` for canary and force a fallback policy mapping so new kernel is opt-in per model. I'll send the rollback PR. :hammer:
ops-bot: Canary rollout paused by @alex at 2024-04-12T15:14:59Z. Rollback ticket created: RB-789. Deployment trigger: https://deploy.redwood-infra/rollbacks/RB-789 :white_check_mark:
jen: We should update the CI perf check to include `kv_miss_rate` and `batch_size_p95` deltas alongside p95 latency. Right now p95 alone misses the routing/batching regressions.
sam: I can sketch the perf probe add — `./ci/perf_probes.yaml` add: `- kv_miss_rate: delta_threshold: 0.05` and `- batch_size_p95: delta_threshold: -0.10` (negative meaning a drop).
maria: After local revert test, I've run a short canary with pinned kernel v1.9 — p95 back within 3% of baseline and KV miss rate stable. I'll push the rollback PR and ask infra to promote.
ryan: Also we should consider a short-term kernel fallback: if kernel choice results in >10% CPU increase for the same token rate, runtime should auto-route to the previous kernel for the affected model id. That avoids manual reverts mid-rollout.
alex: Good call. Feature request: auto-fallback + a canary SLO gate that looks at the 3 metrics (p95, kv_miss_rate, batch_size_p95). If any breach within a 10-min window, trigger a canary pause and optional auto-revert. I'll create a doc for the heuristics.
pat: I'll update the rollout-runbook with steps for bisect + quick attach of flamegraph and alloc snapshot. Keep the bisect template commands.
triage-bot: Perf bisect result posted: bad: 6789abc (kernel-autoselect). Linking: https://ci.redwood-infra/bisects/6789abc
ops-bot: Rollback PR #4330 created by @alex and promoted to canary rollback queue. Deploy started. :shipit:
(8m later)
ops-bot: Rollback to kernel `v1.9-kernel` completed on canary. Post-deploy perf check: p95 within 4% of baseline, kv_miss_rate delta +0.8%, batch_size_p95 delta -2%. :tada:
alex: Thanks team. Next steps: 1) add probes to CI (jen/sam), 2) add runtime auto-fallback (ryan), 3) schedule a deeper perf review of the kernel implementation (maria/sam). I'll sync with infra to prevent simultaneous batching and kernel-change merges for next two weeks. :eyes:
maria: I'll file a follow-up PR to instrument the kernel paths with lightweight tracing so we can correlate memcpy/alloc hotspots automatically.
jen: Noted — I'll also adjust the canary gating thresholds so small regressions (<=5%) don't auto-revert but trigger a higher-fidelity test.
pat: Closing the incident doc and linking RB-789. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
